title: Cat
text:
The cat is a small animal that many people keep as a pet. Cats have soft fur, sharp claws and a long tail.
Cats like to sleep a lot. They can see well at night. A young cat is called a kitten.
History
People have lived with cats for thousands of years.

title: Apple
text:
An apple is a round fruit that grows on a tree. Apples can be red, green or yellow.
People eat apples raw or cook them in pies. Apple juice is made by pressing apples.
Apple trees grow best in places with cold winters.

title: River
text:
A river is a long stream of water that flows across the land. Most rivers flow into a sea, a lake or another river.
Rivers give people water to drink and water for farms. Many big cities were built next to rivers.
Fish, birds and many other animals live in and near rivers.

title: Moon
text:
The Moon is the natural satellite of the Earth. It goes around the Earth about once every month.
The Moon has no air and no water that we can drink. Its ground is covered with gray dust and rocks.
People first walked on the Moon in 1969.

title: Football
text:
Football is a team sport. Two teams of eleven players try to kick a ball into the other team's goal.
Only the goalkeeper may touch the ball with the hands. A game has two halves of forty-five minutes.
Football is the most popular sport in the world.

title: Bread
text:
Bread is a food made from flour and water. Most bread also has yeast, which makes it soft and light.
People have made bread for thousands of years. There are many kinds of bread, like white bread, brown bread and flat bread.

title: Rain
text:
Rain is water that falls from clouds in the sky. It falls when small drops of water in a cloud join together and become heavy. Rain gives water to plants, animals and people. Too much rain at one time can cause floods, and too little rain for a long time can cause a drought. Some places get rain almost every day, while other places, like deserts, get very little rain in a whole year. People measure rain with a tool called a rain gauge, which is a tube that collects the water that falls. Farmers watch the rain closely because their crops need the right amount of water to grow. In many countries, there is a rainy season and a dry season each year. Rain can also wash dirt and dust out of the air, which is why the air often smells fresh after it rains. Rainbows can appear when the sun shines through the rain.

title: Elephant
text:
Elephants are the largest land animals. They have big ears, a long nose called a trunk and two long teeth called tusks.
Elephants live in Africa and Asia. They eat grass, leaves and fruit. An elephant can eat more than one hundred kilograms of food in a day.
Elephants live in family groups led by an old female.

title: Teacher
text:
A teacher is a person who helps other people learn. Most teachers work in schools.
Teachers plan lessons, give homework and help students when they do not understand something. Some teachers teach young children, and others teach adults.

title: Ocean
text:
An ocean is a very large body of salt water. Oceans cover most of the surface of the Earth.
There are five oceans. The biggest one is the Pacific Ocean.
Many kinds of fish, whales and plants live in the oceans.
